## Code quality rules and proactive checks

### Rule 301 : Systematic code quality check before commit

**MANDATORY**: Before creating a commit, ALWAYS perform the following checks:

#### 1. Go linter (golangci-lint)
```bash
golangci-lint run
```

**Required actions:**
- ✅ Fix ALL warnings and errors
- ✅ Specifically check deprecation warnings (SA1019)
- ✅ NEVER ignore warnings without documented justification

#### 2. Tests
```bash
go test ./...
```

**Required actions:**
- ✅ Verify that all tests pass
- ✅ If tests fail, fix them BEFORE the commit

#### 3. Build
```bash
go build
```

**Required actions:**
- ✅ Verify that the build succeeds without errors
- ✅ Test the application if functional changes were made

#### 4. Deprecated dependencies

**Detection:**
- Check golangci-lint SA1019 warnings
- Look in go.mod for packages marked as deprecated

**Action:**
- Replace IMMEDIATELY with a maintained alternative
- Document the replacement in the commit message
- Update the documentation (.claude/CLAUDE.md)

**Examples of common replacements:**
- `github.com/go-ping/ping` → `github.com/prometheus-community/pro-bing`

### Rule 302 : IDE diagnostics check

**MANDATORY**: Before each commit, check the IDE diagnostics:

```
Use mcp__ide__getDiagnostics to check:
- Compilation errors
- Unused parameters
- Unused imports
- Other warnings
```

**Required actions:**
- ✅ Fix or justify every diagnostic
- ✅ Do not ignore "unused parameter" without a reason

### Rule 303 : go.mod and dependencies

**After any dependency change:**

```bash
go mod tidy
go mod verify
```

**Required actions:**
- ✅ Verify that go.mod is up to date
- ✅ Verify that go.sum is consistent
- ✅ Document new dependencies in .claude/CLAUDE.md

### Rule 304 : Quality commit message

**Mandatory format for quality fixes — in English (see Rule 307):**

```
type: short description

Detailed description explaining:
- What was detected (warning, error, etc.)
- Why it was a problem
- How it was resolved

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
```

**Commit types for quality:**
- `fix:` - Bug fix detected by linter
- `chore:` - Deprecated dependency replacement
- `refactor:` - Code quality improvement

### Rule 305 : MANDATORY pre-commit checklist

**Before EVERY commit, check:**

- [ ] `golangci-lint run` → 0 warnings
- [ ] `go test ./...` → PASS
- [ ] `go build` → SUCCESS
- [ ] `mcp__ide__getDiagnostics` → No critical error
- [ ] `go.mod` up to date (if dependencies changed)
- [ ] Documentation updated (if API changed)
- [ ] Tests added (if new feature)

**If EVEN ONE of these checks fails:**
- ❌ DO NOT create the commit
- ✅ Fix it first
- ✅ Restart the checklist

### Rule 306 : MANDATORY proactivity

**Claude Code MUST:**
- ✅ Check the linter WITHOUT the user asking
- ✅ Propose fixes BEFORE the commit
- ✅ Flag deprecated dependencies AS SOON AS they are detected
- ✅ Document all quality changes

**Claude Code MUST NEVER:**
- ❌ Wait for the user to flag a warning
- ❌ Create a commit with unresolved warnings
- ❌ Ignore dependency issues
- ❌ Forget to update the documentation

### Correct workflow examples

**Example 1 - Feature commit:**
```
1. Write the code
2. go build → verify compilation
3. golangci-lint run → fix warnings
4. go test ./... → verify tests
5. mcp__ide__getDiagnostics → check the IDE
6. git commit with a detailed message
```

**Example 2 - Detecting a deprecated dependency:**
```
1. golangci-lint detects SA1019
2. Look up the recommended alternative
3. Replace the import and the code
4. go mod tidy
5. Test that everything works
6. Update .claude/CLAUDE.md
7. git commit explaining the replacement
```

### Rule 307 : Commits and code comments — English only

**Every git commit message and every comment in the code must be written
in English**, regardless of the language used to converse with the user.

| Element | Language |
|---------|--------|
| Commit message (title + body) | ✅ English only |
| Code comment (`//`, `/* */`, docstring) | ✅ English only |
| Replies to the user in the conversation | The user's language (see memory `feedback-langue-francais`) |
| UI and logs (Rule 129) | English US only — already covered, unchanged |

This **replaces** the earlier tolerance listed in `.claude/CLAUDE.md` under
"Code Conventions" ("Comments: French or English both accepted"): existing
French comments are not to be rewritten wholesale, but any new comment and
any edit to an existing comment must be in English.

```
// ✅ CORRECT
// retry with backoff because the API rate-limits bursts above 10 req/s

// ❌ WRONG (a French comment, which Rule 307 forbids)
// on relance avec un backoff car l'API limite les rafales au-delà de 10 req/s
```

```
✅ fix: correct table width calculation when a column is dropped

Bordures étaient soustraites deux fois, ce qui tronquait la dernière colonne.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

❌ fix: corrige le calcul de largeur de colonne
```

Forbidden:
- ❌ A commit message written in French, even partially
- ❌ A new code comment in French
- ❌ Confusing this rule with the language of the conversation, which
  remains the user's

### Rule 302 : IDE diagnostics check

**MANDATORY**: Before each commit, check the IDE diagnostics:

```
Use mcp__ide__getDiagnostics to check:
- Compilation errors
- Unused parameters
- Unused imports
- Other warnings
```

**Required actions:**
- ✅ Fix or justify every diagnostic
- ✅ Do not ignore "unused parameter" without a reason

### Rule 303 : go.mod and dependencies

**After any dependency change:**

```bash
go mod tidy
go mod verify
```

**Required actions:**
- ✅ Verify that go.mod is up to date
- ✅ Verify that go.sum is consistent
- ✅ Document new dependencies in .claude/CLAUDE.md

### Rule 304 : Quality commit message

**Mandatory format for quality fixes — in English (see Rule 307):**

```
type: short description

Detailed description explaining:
- What was detected (warning, error, etc.)
- Why it was a problem
- How it was resolved

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
```

**Commit types for quality:**
- `fix:` - Bug fix detected by linter
- `chore:` - Deprecated dependency replacement
- `refactor:` - Code quality improvement

### Rule 305 : MANDATORY pre-commit checklist

**Before EVERY commit, check:**

- [ ] `golangci-lint run` → 0 warnings
- [ ] `go test ./...` → PASS
- [ ] `go build` → SUCCESS
- [ ] `mcp__ide__getDiagnostics` → No critical error
- [ ] `go.mod` up to date (if dependencies changed)
- [ ] Documentation updated (if API changed)
- [ ] Tests added (if new feature)

**If EVEN ONE of these checks fails:**
- ❌ DO NOT create the commit
- ✅ Fix it first
- ✅ Restart the checklist

### Rule 306 : MANDATORY proactivity

**Claude Code MUST:**
- ✅ Check the linter WITHOUT the user asking
- ✅ Propose fixes BEFORE the commit
- ✅ Flag deprecated dependencies AS SOON AS they are detected
- ✅ Document all quality changes

**Claude Code MUST NEVER:**
- ❌ Wait for the user to flag a warning
- ❌ Create a commit with unresolved warnings
- ❌ Ignore dependency issues
- ❌ Forget to update the documentation

### Correct workflow examples

**Example 1 - Feature commit:**
```
1. Write the code
2. go build → verify compilation
3. golangci-lint run → fix warnings
4. go test ./... → verify tests
5. mcp__ide__getDiagnostics → check the IDE

```

**Example 2 - Detecting a deprecated dependency:**
```

2. Look up the recommended alternative

4. go mod tidy

6. Update .claude/CLAUDE.md

```

### Rule 307 : Commits and code comments — English only

**Every git commit message and every comment in the code must be written
in English**, regardless of the language used to converse with the user.

9	## Vision
10	
11	Dans la vue Network de DevDesk, un onglet « Path » montre, depuis cette machine, par où passe l'appel vers une cible : source, interface de sortie, passerelle, puis chaque saut, avec l'honnêteté d'un outil qui ne prétend jamais répondre pour une autre machine.
12	
13	## Problème
14	
15	- Quand un appel n'atteint pas sa cible, le dev ne sait pas si le problème est **local, dans son réseau ou plus loin** (S-09).
16	- Quand un VPN capture la route par défaut, les checks actuels rapportent le symptôme (pas de réponse ICMP, pas de connexion TCP) ; le stage `route` de `netcheck` nomme l'interface de sortie et la passerelle, mais **rien n'indique les sauts suivants** (code : `runRoute`, `RouteHop{Interface, Source, Gateway}`).
17	- Sous WSL2, le premier saut est un switch virtuel et non un routeur ; sous Docker Desktop, le chemin interne d'un conteneur n'existe pas sur la machine. Un affichage naïf induit en erreur (S-06, S-07).

19	## Pourquoi pas simplement rétablir l'ancien trace

21	`docs/architecture/network.md` (§3.47) explique que l'ancien trace a été **supprimé, pas réécrit** :

Il ne contredit pas la décision de §3.47 : le trace s'exécute **dans le processus DevDesk**, sans conteneur et sans binaire externe. Conséquence à documenter à la livraison : `network.md` devra dire que le trace revient, et pourquoi il répond désormais pour la bonne machine.

1	# Chemin d'un appel réseau : faisabilité et critères binaires du spike
2	
3	> Le rapport WSL (`spike-wsl.md`) est livré par une PR distincte.
4	
5	> Critères binaires L1 à L7 et W1 à W5, lecture des critères d'acceptation de S-01, S-02 et S-03a (stories DEVDESK-325 à DEVDESK-335, `docs/architecture/network.md`, `internal/netiface`, `internal/ports`, stage `route` de `internal/netcheck`) ; ce n'est pas une estimation de l'architecte. Ce qui n'est pas déductible est marqué **À CONFIRMER**.
6	>
7	> Chaque critère donne : un **énoncé binaire** (vrai ou faux, pas « à peu près »), une **méthode de mesure**, et l'**effet de l'échec**, fixé avant de mesurer. Tous les effets sont **Décidés** : soit par une story ou la règle go/no-go du brief, soit par l'utilisateur (arbitrage du 2026-11-12, repris ci-dessous).
8	
9	## Verdict de faisabilité
10	
11	**Avant le spike : plausible, à mesurer.** Sur Linux, un socket UDP non privilégié avec `IP_TTL` et `IP_RECVERR` reçoit, dans sa file d'erreurs, les ICMP Time Exceeded avec l'adresse du routeur : c'était l'hypothèse H1 des stories, tenue pour non acquise.
12	
13	**Après le spike.** Linux natif (Debian 13, noyau 6.12) : **fonctionne**, L1 à L7 OK (`spike-linux.md`). WSL2 en NAT et en mirrored : **supporté, avec réserves**, W1 OK dans les deux modes, mode distinguable (W2) ; réserves : pas de preuve que le premier saut est l'hôte Windows en mirrored (W3), pas de conteneur réel observé pour W5 (`spike-wsl.md`). Les mesures WSL2 ont été faites dans la distro WSL par l'équipe d'agents ; l'utilisateur a basculé le mode.
14	
15	Déjà acquis par la lecture du code :
16	
17	- le stage `route` donne interface, adresse source et passerelle sans privilège, ~2 ms (`Env.Route` -> `RouteHop{Interface, Source, Gateway}`, `go-netroute`) ;
18	- `internal/netiface.List` donne les interfaces de **cette machine** sans conteneur ; il suffit à tester l'existence d'un bridge par son nom ;
19	- WSL se reconnaît déjà par `WSL_DISTRO_NAME` dans `internal/browser`, `internal/clipboard` et `internal/ui/terminal` (même signal) ; `/proc/version` est cité par S-02 comme second signal ; le mode (NAT ou mirrored) se lit par `wslinfo --networking-mode` (constat, `spike-wsl.md`, W2) ;
20	- `golang.org/x/sys v0.49.0` est dans `go.mod` en `// indirect` ; il passe en dépendance directe (décidé, voir conditions de mesure).
21	
22	## Conditions de mesure communes (S-01, S-02)
23	
24	- Le prototype est **un binaire autonome**, lançable sur un autre poste (S-01) : `CGO_ENABLED=0`, `file` / `ldd` le disent statique ; son rapport est **collable tel quel** (S-01).
25	- Le rapport donne : OS, version du noyau, version de Go, mode réseau (pour WSL), la cible, le détail de chaque mesure, et pour chaque critère « OK / KO » avec l'effet décidé ici.
26	- Le prototype est lancé en **utilisateur sans privilège** (UID différent de 0, `CapEff` vide, lu dans `/proc/self/status` et consigné par le binaire).
27	- La cible publique est un **paramètre** du binaire, jamais codé en dur, et consignée dans le rapport. **Cible de référence : `1.1.1.1`. Décidé.**

36	## Règle d'effet par défaut
37	
38	L'échec d'un critère L signifie « S-01 ne fonctionne pas » => **Epic B abandonné** (S-01), sauf si la ligne du critère prévoit un plan B, un assouplissement ou une correction (L3, L6, L7). Pour un critère W, l'effet est borné à WSL2 : **WSL2 est grisé** (S-02, S-08), à condition que Linux natif ait réussi. Si W2 conclut que le mode est indistinguable, ou si **un seul** des deux modes échoue à W1, **WSL2 entier est grisé** (décision du 2026-11-12, voir W1 et W2).

42	## Linux natif : L1 à L7
43	
44	### L1. Sans privilège, sans binaire externe, sans conteneur
45	
46	- **Énoncé.** Un utilisateur sans privilège (UID != 0, `CapEff` = 0) peut ouvrir un socket UDP, y positionner `IP_TTL` et `IP_RECVERR`, et émettre une sonde ; le binaire n'exécute aucun programme externe ni conteneur.
47	- **Méthode.** (a) Lancer le binaire sous un compte ordinaire sans `setcap` ni `sudo` ; le rapport consigne UID et `CapEff`. (b) Le paquet de trace n'importe pas `os/exec` (inspection de ses imports directs : `go list -f '{{.Imports}}'`). (c) Lancer avec `PATH` vide et sans moteur de conteneurs disponible : le résultat est identique. (d) `setsockopt` réussit sans `EPERM` (le rapport consigne l'erreur éventuelle, texte brut dans le détail, jamais dans un résumé affichable, Rule 129).
48	- **Effet de l'échec.** S-01 ne fonctionne pas => Epic B abandonné. **Décidé** (S-01 : « sans privilège, sans dépendance externe et sans conteneur »).
49	
50	### L2. Réception des Time Exceeded : au moins 3 sauts avec adresse
51	
52	- **Énoncé.** Vers une cible publique, le prototype obtient **au moins 3 sauts**, chacun avec l'adresse du routeur qui a répondu, rendus dans l'ordre croissant de TTL.
53	- **Méthode.** Une sonde par TTL ; le Time Exceeded est lu dans la file d'erreurs (`recvmsg` avec `MSG_ERRQUEUE`) et l'adresse du routeur est celle de l'émetteur de l'erreur (`sock_extended_err` / offender). Chaque sonde est reliée à son TTL (par socket ou par port : choix du spike). Rapport : TTL, adresse, latence. Un saut à adresse privée compte comme un saut.
54	- **Effet de l'échec.** S-01 ne fonctionne pas => Epic B abandonné. **Décidé** (S-01, critère 1).
55	
56	### L3. Netpoller Go
57	
58	- **Énoncé.** L'attente de la file d'erreurs rend la main **sur l'arrivée de l'erreur**, sans boucle d'attente active ; si ce n'est pas le cas, le plan B (socket bloquant avec délai de lecture) tient les mesures L5 et L6.
59	- **Méthode.** Lecture par `RawConn.Read` (le netpoller de Go) avec un délai de lecture large. Pour chaque sonde qui a reçu une réponse, le temps d'attente est de l'ordre de la latence mesurée, **très inférieur au délai** (le délai n'a pas réveillé la lecture). Aucune boucle `time.Sleep` / polling dans le code de lecture. Si la lecture ne se réveille pas : refaire L5 et L6 avec le plan B et consigner lequel des deux chemins est retenu.
60	- **Effet de l'échec.** Plan B retenu, **pas de no-go**. Si le plan B échoue aussi à L5 ou L6, c'est l'échec de L5 ou L6. **Décidé** (S-01, hypothèse 2).
61	
62	### L4. Saut muet
63	
64	- **Énoncé.** Un routeur qui ne répond pas est rapporté **muet** (avec son TTL) sans arrêter le trace avant la cible : les TTL suivants sont encore sondés et rapportés.
65	- **Méthode.** Soit un chemin réel contenant un saut muet, soit un laboratoire : espace de noms réseau avec un routeur qui jette ses ICMP Time Exceeded (la mise en place demande des droits, **pas le prototype**, qui reste sans privilège). **Cas net (définition stricte) : un routeur muet puis un routeur qui répond.** « Muet puis cible » n'est pas un cas net : les TTL muets entre le dernier routeur et la cible atteinte sont des sondes qui ont atteint la cible. Le rapport montre au moins un cas net. Une exécution sans cas net est neutre (décision 9).
66	- **Effet de l'échec.** S-01 ne fonctionne pas => Epic B abandonné. **Décidé** (utilisateur, 2026-11-12 : L4 bloquant).
67	
68	### L5. Arrêt en 30 s au plus avec résultat explicite
69	
70	- **Énoncé.** Vers une cible inatteignable (ou si le TTL maximum est atteint), le prototype s'arrête en **au plus 30 s** et rend un résultat explicite qui distingue « cible atteinte », « cible non atteinte, TTL maximum » et « cible non atteinte, délai écoulé ».
71	- **Méthode.** Mesure de l'horloge murale (`time`) sur une cible qui ne répond pas (par exemple une adresse du bloc de documentation `192.0.2.0/24`, jamais routée sur Internet). Cas « TTL maximum » : faute de cible dont le chemin dépasse réellement 30 sauts, TTL maximum abaissé à 5 vers `1.1.1.1`, et cible muette `192.0.2.1` (décision 10). Cas « délai écoulé » : configuration inversée, durée de sonde supérieure au délai global (par exemple sonde de 20 s, délai global de 1,5 s). Rapport : durée, résultat. Pas de seuil intermédiaire.
72	- **Effet de l'échec.** S-01 ne fonctionne pas => Epic B abandonné. **Décidé** (utilisateur, 2026-11-12 : L5 bloquant).
73	
74	### L6. 8 sauts en moins de 5 s, sondes en parallèle
75	
76	- **Énoncé.** Vers une cible joignable à 8 sauts, le résultat est **complet en moins de 5 s**, parce que les sondes de tous les TTL partent en parallèle.
77	- **Méthode.** Cible de référence `1.1.1.1`. On relève d'abord le TTL de la cible atteinte N (chemin réel présumé : N n'est pas toujours le nombre réel de sauts, voir `spike-linux.md`) : **si N est au moins 8, la mesure porte sur ce chemin** (les 8 premiers TTL au moins, résultat complet) ; **sinon le TTL est borné à 8** et la borne est consignée. Durée entre le lancement et le résultat complet, sur 5 exécutions, valeurs min / médiane / max consignées. La durée de sonde choisie est consignée ; elle doit rester inférieure à 5 s, y compris quand un saut est muet.
78	- **Effet de l'échec.** **Pas de no-go : on assouplit le seuil de S-03a** (le critère « moins de 5 s » est réécrit à partir des durées mesurées). **Décidé** (utilisateur, 2026-11-12). Si le seuil ne peut pas être réécrit parce que les sondes ne sont pas réellement parallèles (durée proche de la somme des délais), c'est un défaut de conception du prototype : corriger puis re-mesurer.
79	
80	### L7. Annulation sans fuite de sockets
81	
82	- **Énoncé.** Un trace en cours, annulé (contexte annulé), s'arrête et **ne laisse ni descripteur ni goroutine** derrière lui.
83	- **Méthode.** Annuler en plein trace (une sonde muette en attente), sur 100 cycles consécutifs. Comparer avant et après : nombre d'entrées de `/proc/self/fd` et `runtime.NumGoroutine()`. Aucune croissance. Consigner le délai d'arrêt après annulation (sans seuil : les stories n'en fixent pas).
84	- **Effet de l'échec.** Correction du prototype puis re-mesure ; **no-go seulement si la fuite est structurelle** (impossible à fermer avec l'API retenue). **Décidé** (utilisateur, 2026-11-12). Le rapport consigne la fuite, la correction et la mesure suivante.
85	
86	### Verdict S-01
87	
88	**Fonctionne** si L1 à L7 sont OK (L3 par le netpoller ou par le plan B). **Ne fonctionne pas** sinon, avec l'effet de chaque ligne en échec. Le verdict, le tableau L1 à L7 et les mesures sont écrits dans `docs/product/network-map/spike-linux.md` (S-01).

92	## WSL2 : W1 à W5 (S-02)
93	
94	Chaque critère est évalué **pour chaque mode** (NAT, puis mirrored) et consigné séparément. La mesure est faite dans la distro WSL2 du poste Windows, par l'équipe d'agents ; l'utilisateur bascule le mode réseau. Les résultats vont dans `docs/product/network-map/spike-wsl.md`.
95	
96	### W1. Mêmes mesures en NAT et en mirrored
97	
98	- **Énoncé.** Dans le mode considéré, L1 à L7 sont tous OK.
99	- **Méthode.** Lancer le binaire de S-01 dans la distro WSL2 sous chaque mode. Rapport par mode : verdict L1 à L7 et premier saut. Risque connu à surveiller : en mirrored, les Time Exceeded peuvent ne jamais arriver (S-02).
100	- **Effet de l'échec.** Un mode en échec grise **WSL2 entier** (S-08), car le mode actif n'est pas toujours distinguable (W2) ; on livre pour Linux natif. **Décidé** (S-02, règle go/no-go du brief, puis utilisateur 2026-11-12 : WSL2 entier). Si **les deux** modes échouent et que Linux natif réussit, on livre pour Linux natif seul et **le rapport (`spike-wsl.md`) l'écrit explicitement** : le poste WSL2 de l'utilisateur n'est alors pas couvert. **Décidé.**
101	
102	### W2. Détection de WSL et de son mode
103	
104	- **Énoncé.** Le rapport établit, pour chaque mode, que l'environnement est WSL2 et **quel mode** est actif, par un signal qui distingue NAT de mirrored ; sinon il constate que le mode n'est pas distinguable.
105	- **Méthode.** Consigner `WSL_DISTRO_NAME`, le contenu de `/proc/version`, les interfaces et adresses (comme `internal/netiface`), la route par défaut, `/etc/resolv.conf`, et tout autre signal que le spike trouve. **Constat** (`spike-wsl.md`) : `wslinfo --networking-mode` (dans la distro) rend `nat` ou `mirrored` ; l'interface et la route par défaut diffèrent aussi. Le critère est vrai si au moins un signal donne des valeurs **différentes et stables** entre les deux modes sur toutes les exécutions.
106	- **Effet de l'échec.** Mode « indéterminé » : la colonne affiche `WSL2 mode undetermined` sans deviner et S-07 passe de S à M. **Décidé** (S-07 : critère et contexte d'effort). Si le mode est indistinguable, **WSL2 entier est grisé** (le mode en échec ne peut pas être exclu). **Décidé** (utilisateur, 2026-11-12). Le signal de détection est établi par le spike : `wslinfo --networking-mode` (WSL 2.7.13.0).
107	
108	### W3. Le premier saut est l'hôte Windows
109	
110	- **Énoncé.** L'adresse du premier saut (TTL 1) est identifiée comme l'hôte Windows par une **preuve reproductible**.
111	- **Méthode.** Comparer l'adresse du TTL 1 à la passerelle de la route par défaut de la distro (la même information que le stage `route`) et à l'interface de sortie. En NAT : la passerelle du NAT est le switch virtuel de l'hôte Windows (S-07) ; consigner la preuve utilisée. En mirrored : consigner si une preuve existe. « Pas de réponse au TTL 1 » est un résultat, consigné tel quel.
112	- **Effet de l'échec.** NAT sans preuve : pas d'étiquette `Windows host (virtual switch)`. Mirrored sans preuve : la passerelle n'est pas étiquetée hôte Windows (**Décidé**, S-07, critère mirrored).
113	
114	### W4. Nature du `docker` visible depuis la distro
115	
116	- **Énoncé.** Le rapport établit, **sans ambiguïté**, si le `docker` visible est Docker Desktop (binaire sous `/mnt/c/…`) ou un Engine installé dans la distro.
117	- **Méthode.** Chemin résolu du binaire `docker` (`command -v docker`, lien résolu), présence d'un démon dans la distro, et réponse de l'engine sur son nom et son système. **Constat** (`spike-wsl.md`) : l'intégration WSL de Docker Desktop expose le client sous `/mnt/wsl/docker-desktop/cli-tools/usr/bin/docker`, pas sous `/mnt/c/…` que cite S-02. Le critère est un **constat** : « non établi » est l'échec.
118	- **Effet de l'échec.** La colonne indique le doute plutôt que de deviner. **Décidé** (S-06, critère 4).
119	
120	### W5. Bridge d'un conteneur côté distro
121	
122	- **Énoncé.** Le rapport établit si le bridge du réseau d'un conteneur de test **existe** dans les interfaces lues dans la distro.
123	- **Méthode.** L'utilisateur lance à la main un conteneur sur le réseau par défaut puis sur un réseau défini ; le binaire liste les interfaces (`net.Interfaces`, comme `internal/netiface`) et compare à l'engine. Répéter pour chaque nature d'engine trouvée en W4 et pour chaque mode. Le critère est un **constat** : « non établi » est l'échec.
124	- **Effet de l'échec.** Bridge absent : aucun bridge n'est affiché, et le cas Docker Desktop passe par l'étape `Engine VM` (**Décidé**, S-05b et S-06). Bridge présent : il est une étape entre le conteneur et l'hôte (**Décidé**, S-05b).
125	
126	### Verdict S-02
127	
128	Un verdict **par mode** : « fonctionne » si W1 est OK, avec les constats W2 à W5. **Le verdict d'ensemble est « WSL2 supporté » seulement si les deux modes fonctionnent et que le mode est distinguable (W2) ; sinon WSL2 entier est grisé** (décidé). Si les deux modes échouent et que Linux natif est OK, le rapport l'écrit en toutes lettres. Les constats déterminent S-07 (étiquettes, effort S ou M), S-06 (boîte noire) et S-08 (WSL2 grisé).

125	)
126	
127	// String returns the outcome in US English.
128	func (o Outcome) String() string {
129		switch o {
130		case OutcomeReached:
131			return "reached"
132		case OutcomeMaxHops:
133			return "max hops"
134		case OutcomeDeadline:
135			return "deadline"
136		case OutcomeCancelled:
137			return "canceled"
138		case OutcomeUnreachable:
139			return "unreachable"
140		}
141		return "unknown"
142	}
143	
144	// Result is a finished trace.
145	//
146	// Hops is cut at the terminal hop (target reached or refused) or, when the
147	// trace ends at MaxHops, holds one hop per TTL. When a cancellation or the
148	// deadline ends it first, Hops holds exactly MaxHops entries, Hops[i].TTL ==
149	// i+1, and every probe that did not resolve is a HopUnresolved; so even with a
150	// terminal hop already known, the TTLs above it can show up as HopUnresolved.
151	// The probes above the target are all sent: only their wait is cut short.
152	//
153	// Always check the error Trace returned before
154	// reading it: the zero Result (and so the zero Outcome, OutcomeReached) means
155	// "no trace", never "reached".
156	type Result struct {
157		Target   netip.Addr
158		Outcome  Outcome
159		Hops     []Hop
160		Duration time.Duration
161	}
162	
163	// Supported reports whether this platform can trace: nil, or ErrUnsupported.
164	func Supported() error {
165		return supported()
166	}
167	
168	// Trace probes the path to target. An IPv4-mapped IPv6 target is converted to
169	// IPv4; any other non-IPv4 target gets ErrNotIPv4 and nothing is sent. An
170	// unspecified (0.0.0.0), multicast or limited broadcast (255.255.255.255)
171	// target gets ErrNotUnicast. Subnet broadcasts cannot be told apart and are not
172	// checked. Loopback and private addresses are allowed: whether tracing them is
173	// acceptable is the caller's decision, at its own boundary.
174	//
175	// The errors Trace returns and Hop.Err carry raw platform text (errno
176	// messages): match the sentinels with errors.Is and show fixed labels, never
177	// that text in a summary.
178	func Trace(ctx context.Context, target netip.Addr, opts Options) (Result, error) {
179		if err := supported(); err != nil {
180			return Result{}, err
181		}
182		target = target.Unmap()
183		if !target.Is4() {
184			return Result{}, ErrNotIPv4
185		}
186		if target.IsUnspecified() || target.IsMulticast() || target == netip.AddrFrom4([4]byte{255, 255, 255, 255}) {
187			return Result{}, ErrNotUnicast
188		}
189		return run(ctx, target, opts, systemProber())
190	}

2	// the DevDesk process.
3	//
4	// The trace used to need a container (or a traceroute binary) because probing
5	// with a chosen TTL and reading what the routers answer takes more than the
6	// standard library offers. Here the process does it itself: one connected UDP
7	// socket per TTL, with IP_TTL set and IP_RECVERR enabled, then a read of the
8	// socket's error queue for the ICMP answer. No raw ICMP socket is opened, so
9	// nothing is started and no container is needed. The package never starts a
10	// child process (see the source guard test).
11	//
12	// The probes use connected sockets with an ephemeral source port, so an ICMP
13	// message forged off the path can at worst skew what is displayed; it cannot
14	// make the trace read anything else.
15	//
16	// Only Linux is supported: elsewhere Supported and Trace return ErrUnsupported
17	// and the caller is expected to grey the feature out.

11	
12	// unsupportedProber opens nothing: Trace stops at supported() first.
13	type unsupportedProber struct{}
14	
15	func (unsupportedProber) open(context.Context, netip.Addr, int) (probeConn, error) {
16		return nil, ErrUnsupported
17	}
18	
19	// systemProber returns a prober that never opens a connection.
20	func systemProber() prober { return unsupportedProber{} }

## Code editing instructions

### Rule 201 : Code must be clean, concise, and well-structured to stay maintainable

#### Extracting functions from Update()
- **Strict limit**: If a case in `Update(msg tea.Msg)` exceeds **5 lines**, extract it into a separate function
- **Naming**: `handle[MessageType]` (e.g. `handleContextSwitch()`, `handleKeyPress()`)
- **Pattern**: The function must return `(tea.Model, tea.Cmd)`

**Before (bad):**
```go
case ContextSwitchCompleteMsg:
    a.config = msg.Config
    a.currentContext = msg.ContextName
    a.reinitializeViews(msg.Config)
    return a, func() tea.Msg {
        return tea.WindowSizeMsg{Width: a.width, Height: a.height}
    }
```

**After (good):**
```go
case ContextSwitchCompleteMsg:
    return a.handleContextSwitch(msg)

// Further down in the file
func (a *App) handleContextSwitch(msg ContextSwitchCompleteMsg) (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {
    a.config = msg.Config
    a.currentContext = msg.ContextName
    a.reinitializeViews(msg.Config)
    return a, func() tea.Msg {
        return tea.WindowSizeMsg{Width: a.width, Height: a.height}
    }
}
```

#### Code reuse
- **Zero duplication**: If a block of code appears 2+ times, create a function
- **Modules**: Group related functions together (e.g. all context switching in a single file)
- **Constants**: Extract magic values into named constants

#### Error handling
- **Bubble Tea pattern**: Errors = messages (e.g. `ContextSwitchErrorMsg`)
- **Always log** in DEBUG mode: `log.Printf("ERROR: %v", err)`
- **Never ignore**: If the error is non-critical, document why

#### Comments
- **Mandatory for**:
  - Exported (public) functions
  - Complex business logic
  - Workarounds or non-obvious decisions
- **Format**: `// functionName does X and returns Y`
- **Avoid**: Comments that repeat the code

#### Complexity
- **Maximum 3 levels of indentation** in a function
- **Functions > 50 lines**: refactor into smaller functions
- **Switch > 10 cases**: consider a table-driven pattern

</system-reminder>

## Code quality rules and proactive checks

### Rule 301 : Systematic code quality check before commit

**MANDATORY**: Before creating a commit, ALWAYS perform the following checks:

#### 1. Go linter (golangci-lint)
```bash
golangci-lint run
```

**Required actions:**
- ✅ Fix ALL warnings and errors
- ✅ Specifically check deprecation warnings (SA1019)
- ✅ NEVER ignore warnings without documented justification

#### 2. Tests
```bash
go test ./...
```

**Required actions:**
- ✅ Verify that all tests pass
- ✅ If tests fail, fix them BEFORE the commit

#### 3. Build
```bash
go build
```

**Required actions:**
- ✅ Verify that the build succeeds without errors
- ✅ Test the application if functional changes were made

#### 4. Deprecated dependencies

**Detection:**
- Check golangci-lint SA1019 warnings
- Look in go.mod for packages marked as deprecated

**Action:**
- Replace IMMEDIATELY with a maintained alternative
- Document the replacement in the commit message
- Update the documentation (.claude/CLAUDE.md)

**Examples of common replacements:**
- `github.com/go-ping/ping` → `github.com/prometheus-community/pro-bing`

### Rule 302 : IDE diagnostics check

**MANDATORY**: Before each commit, check the IDE diagnostics:

```
Use mcp__ide__getDiagnostics to check:
- Compilation errors
- Unused parameters
- Unused imports
- Other warnings
```

**Required actions:**
- ✅ Fix or justify every diagnostic
- ✅ Do not ignore "unused parameter" without a reason

### Rule 303 : go.mod and dependencies

**After any dependency change:**

```bash
go mod tidy
go mod verify
```

**Required actions:**
- ✅ Verify that go.mod is up to date
- ✅ Verify that go.sum is consistent
- ✅ Document new dependencies in .claude/CLAUDE.md

### Rule 304 : Quality commit message

**Mandatory format for quality fixes — in English (see Rule 307):**

```
type: short description

Detailed description explaining:
- What was detected (warning, error, etc.)
- Why it was a problem
- How it was resolved

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
```

**Commit types for quality:**
- `fix:` - Bug fix detected by linter
- `chore:` - Deprecated dependency replacement
- `refactor:` - Code quality improvement

### Rule 305 : MANDATORY pre-commit checklist

**Before EVERY commit, check:**

- [ ] `golangci-lint run` → 0 warnings
- [ ] `go test ./...` → PASS
- [ ] `go build` → SUCCESS
- [ ] `mcp__ide__getDiagnostics` → No critical error
- [ ] `go.mod` up to date (if dependencies changed)
- [ ] Documentation updated (if API changed)
- [ ] Tests added (if new feature)

**If EVEN ONE of these checks fails:**
- ❌ DO NOT create the commit
- ✅ Fix it first
- ✅ Restart the checklist

### Rule 306 : MANDATORY proactivity

**Claude Code MUST:**
- ✅ Check the linter WITHOUT the user asking
- ✅ Propose fixes BEFORE the commit
- ✅ Flag deprecated dependencies AS SOON AS they are detected
- ✅ Document all quality changes

**Claude Code MUST NEVER:**
- ❌ Wait for the user to flag a warning
- ❌ Create a commit with unresolved warnings
- ❌ Ignore dependency issues
- ❌ Forget to update the documentation

### Correct workflow examples

**Example 1 - Feature commit:**
```
1. Write the code
2. go build → verify compilation
3. golangci-lint run → fix warnings
4. go test ./... → verify tests
5. mcp__ide__getDiagnostics → check the IDE
6. git commit with a detailed message
```

**Example 2 - Detecting a deprecated dependency:**
```
1. golangci-lint detects SA1019
2. Look up the recommended alternative
3. Replace the import and the code
4. go mod tidy
5. Test that everything works
6. Update .claude/CLAUDE.md
7. git commit explaining the replacement
```

### Rule 307 : Commits and code comments — English only

**Every git commit message and every comment in the code must be written
in English**, regardless of the language used to converse with the user.

| Element | Language |
|---------|--------|
| Commit message (title + body) | ✅ English only |
| Code comment (`//`, `/* */`, docstring) | ✅ English only |
| Replies to the user in the conversation | The user's language (see memory `feedback-langue-francais`) |
| UI and logs (Rule 129) | English US only — already covered, unchanged |

This **replaces** the earlier tolerance listed in `.claude/CLAUDE.md` under
"Code Conventions" ("Comments: French or English both accepted"): existing
French comments are not to be rewritten wholesale, but any new comment and
any edit to an existing comment must be in English.

```
// ✅ CORRECT
// retry with backoff because the API rate-limits bursts above 10 req/s

// ❌ WRONG (a French comment, which Rule 307 forbids)
// on relance avec un backoff car l'API limite les rafales au-delà de 10 req/s
```

```
✅ fix: correct table width calculation when a column is dropped

Bordures étaient soustraites deux fois, ce qui tronquait la dernière colonne.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

❌ fix: corrige le calcul de largeur de colonne
```

Forbidden:
- ❌ A commit message written in French, even partially
- ❌ A new code comment in French
- ❌ Confusing this rule with the language of the conversation, which
  remains the user's

64	//
65	// The accumulated Results travels *in the message* rather than being mutated in
66	// place: the model holds the previous value while the next stage runs on a
67	// goroutine, so sharing one would be a data race on exactly what Rule 110
68	// forbids. netcheck.RunStep copies for this reason.
69	type stageDoneMsg struct {
70		gen     int // must match Model.runGen; a superseded run's results are discarded
71		stage   netcheck.StageID
72		next    int // index into netcheck.Steps() of the stage still to run
73		results netcheck.Results
74	}

76	// Model represents the network diagnostics view
77	type Model struct {
78		config *config.Config
79		width  int
80		height int
81	
82		// Active tab (tabDiagnostics, tabPorts, tabInterfaces or tabForward)
83		activeTab       int
84		portsModel      *PortsModel
85		interfacesModel *InterfacesModel
86		forwardModel    *ForwardModel
87	
88		state ViewState
89	
90		// Form inputs
91		targetInput    textinput.Model
92		portInput      textinput.Model
93		dnsServerInput textinput.Model
94		focusedField   int
95	
96		// Running state
97		runGen     int // incremented each run; results from a superseded run are dropped
98		runStage   netcheck.StageID
99		runStep    int
100		totalSteps int
101	
102		// Results
103		results     netcheck.Results
104		verdict     netcheck.Verdict
105		checksTable datatable.Model[netcheck.Check]
106		filterBar   components.FilterBar
107	
108		// Details: one check explained
109		detailsViewport viewport.Model
110		selected        netcheck.Check
111	
112		// footer is the one line of transient state below the tab bar (Rule 128).
113		footer components.FooterMessage
114	
115		// OriginView is where esc returns to from StateResults, when set. Empty
116		// means netdiag was opened directly (the command line), and esc there
117		// stays inside the view — resetting to the form, as it always has.
118		OriginView command.ViewType
119	}

121	// New creates a new netdiag view
122	func New(cfg *config.Config) *Model {
123		targetIn := textinput.New()
124		theme.StyleTextInput(&targetIn)
125		targetIn.Placeholder = "hostname or IP address"
126		targetIn.CharLimit = 256
127		targetIn.Focus()
128	
129		portIn := textinput.New()
130		theme.StyleTextInput(&portIn)
131		portIn.Placeholder = defaultPort
132		portIn.CharLimit = 10
133	
134		dnsIn := textinput.New()
135		theme.StyleTextInput(&dnsIn)
136		// Empty means the system resolver, and that is the answer the user cares
137		// about: it is the one their own traffic uses. The old default read the
138		// first nameserver out of /etc/resolv.conf, which does not exist on Windows.
139		dnsIn.Placeholder = "system resolver"
140		dnsIn.CharLimit = 64
141	
142		return &Model{
143			config:          cfg,
144			state:           StateInput,
145			activeTab:       tabDiagnostics,
146			portsModel:      newPortsModel(time.Duration(cfg.Network.PortsRefreshInterval) * time.Second),
147			interfacesModel: newInterfacesModel(),
148			forwardModel:    newForwardModel(),
149			targetInput:     targetIn,
150			portInput:       portIn,
151			dnsServerInput:  dnsIn,
152			focusedField:    fieldTarget,
153			filterBar:       components.NewFilterBarWithTokens([]components.FilterToken{{Label: problemsToken}}),
154			checksTable: datatable.New(datatable.Config[netcheck.Check]{
155				Columns: checkColumns(),
156				// Pipeline order is content: resolve, reach, connect, TLS, HTTP is
157				// the order the questions depend on one another. A table that
158				// reorders itself destroys the one thing the layout says.
159				SortColumn: -1,
160			}),
161		}
162	}
163	
164	// NewWithTarget builds a view prefilled from an already-known target, for a
165	// producer elsewhere in the application (status's H, §3.66) rather than a
166	// user typing into the form. It stays a pure constructor — no tea.Cmd side
167	// effects — so the caller decides whether to also start the run, the same
168	// way uiviewer.NewWithSource hands back a model without loading anything.
169	func NewWithTarget(cfg *config.Config, t netcheck.Target) *Model {
170		m := New(cfg)
171		m.targetInput.SetValue(t.Host)
172		if t.Port > 0 {
173			m.portInput.SetValue(strconv.Itoa(t.Port))
174		}
175		m.dnsServerInput.SetValue(t.Resolver)
176		return m
177	}
178	
179	// buildTarget assembles what the form describes.
180	func (m *Model) buildTarget() (netcheck.Target, error) {
181		host := strings.TrimSpace(m.targetInput.Value())
182		if err := validateTarget(host); err != nil {
183			return netcheck.Target{}, err
184		}
185		port := strings.TrimSpace(m.portInput.Value())
186		if port == "" {
187			port = defaultPort
188		}
189		if err := validatePort(port); err != nil {
190			return netcheck.Target{}, err
191		}
192		n, _ := strconv.Atoi(port) // validatePort has already accepted it
193		return netcheck.Target{
194			Host:     host,
195			Port:     n,
196			Resolver: strings.TrimSpace(m.dnsServerInput.Value()),
197		}, nil
198	}
199	
200	// visibleChecks applies the filter bar to the results.
201	//
202	// The view filters and calls SetItems rather than leaning on the table's own
203	// search, for the reason security and status do: this decides which rows exist
204	// at all, where a FilterBar query narrows a list that is already settled.
205	func (m *Model) visibleChecks() []netcheck.Check {
206		all := m.results.All()
207		query := strings.ToLower(m.filterBar.SearchQuery())
208		onlyProblems := m.filterBar.IsTokenActive(problemsToken)
209	
210		out := make([]netcheck.Check, 0, len(all))
211		for _, c := range all {
212			if onlyProblems && (c.Verdict == netcheck.OK || c.Verdict == netcheck.NotApplicable) {
213				continue
214			}
215			if query != "" && !matchesQuery(c, query) {
216				continue
217			}
218			out = append(out, c)
219		}
220		return out
221	}
222	
223	func matchesQuery(c netcheck.Check, query string) bool {
224		return strings.Contains(strings.ToLower(c.Title), query) ||
225			strings.Contains(strings.ToLower(c.Summary), query)
226	}
227	
228	// checkSettings is what the config says the pipeline should wait for and send.
229	//
230	// Read on every run rather than captured at construction: the configuration
231	// view rebuilds this model on save, but a run already in flight holds its own
232	// copy through the message chain, and taking the values here keeps the two from
233	// disagreeing halfway down the pipeline.
234	//
235	// netcheck.Settings.normalize fills in anything non-positive, so a hand-edited
236	// zero becomes the default rather than a dial with no deadline.
237	func (m *Model) checkSettings() netcheck.Settings {
238		return netcheck.Settings{
239			CheckTimeout:     time.Duration(m.config.Network.CheckTimeout) * time.Second,
240			PingCount:        m.config.Network.PingCount,
241			ExpiryWarnWindow: time.Duration(m.config.Network.CertExpiryWarnDays) * 24 * time.Hour,
242		}
243	}

17	// Init implements tea.Model
18	func (m *Model) Init() tea.Cmd {
19		return tea.Batch(
20			textinput.Blink,
21			m.portsModel.initPorts(),
22			m.interfacesModel.initInterfaces(),
23			// The forwards live on the router, which broadcasts when they change.
24			// A view built after the last change was not there for it, so it asks
25			// once on the way in — the role sendJobsTo plays for the job registry.
26			forward.Refresh,
27		)
28	}

30	// Running reports whether a diagnostic is walking its stages now, which is what
31	// the router asks before it would rebuild the view: dropping it mid-run would
32	// discard the run without a word.
33	func (m *Model) Running() bool { return m.state == StateRunning }
34	
35	// InEditMode implements FormView — true when a text input is active, so the
36	// router hands the key to the field rather than opening the command line.
37	func (m *Model) InEditMode() bool {
38		switch m.activeTab {
39		case tabPorts:
40			return m.portsModel.InEditMode()
41		case tabInterfaces:
42			// The interfaces table has a search box now, where the Topology tab it
43			// replaced had no input at all. Returning false here would let a ":"
44			// typed into the query open the command line instead (Rule 111).
45			return m.interfacesModel.InEditMode()
46		case tabForward:
47			return m.forwardModel.InEditMode()
48		}
49		if m.filterBar.InEditMode() {
50			return true
51		}
52		if m.state == StateInput {
53			return m.focusedField == fieldTarget || m.focusedField == fieldPort || m.focusedField == fieldDNSServer
54		}
55		return false
56	}

58	// FilterBarVisible implements app.FilterBarView.
59	func (m *Model) FilterBarVisible() bool {
60		switch m.activeTab {
61		case tabPorts:
62			return m.portsModel.table.FilterBar().IsVisible()
63		case tabForward:
64			return m.forwardModel.table.FilterBar().IsVisible()
65		}
66		return m.activeTab == tabDiagnostics && m.filterBar.IsVisible()

69	// Update implements tea.Model
70	func (m *Model) Update(msg tea.Msg) (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {
71		switch msg := msg.(type) {
72		case tea.WindowSizeMsg:
73			m.width = msg.Width
74			m.height = msg.Height
75			m.resizeInputs()
76			m.filterBar.Resize(msg.Width)
77			m.rebuildChecksTable()
78			m.resizeDetailsViewport()
79			m.portsModel.resize(msg.Width, msg.Height)
80			m.interfacesModel.resize(msg.Width, msg.Height)
81			m.forwardModel.resize(msg.Width, msg.Height)
82			return m, nil
83	
84		// The router's animation frame: the blink phase of the Ports dot and of the
85		// two footers that show the shared activity dot, whichever tab is on screen
86		// so a tab never comes back with a frozen phase.
87		case jobs.FrameMsg:
88			m.portsModel.table.SetBlinkPhase(msg.Blink)
89			m.footer.SetBlinkPhase(msg.Blink)
90			m.interfacesModel.footer.SetBlinkPhase(msg.Blink)
91			return m, nil
92	
93		case stageDoneMsg:
94			return m.handleStageDone(msg)
95	
96		// Ports sub-model messages.
97		case portsTickMsg, portsDataMsg, portsKillResultMsg:
98			var cmd tea.Cmd
99			m.portsModel, cmd = m.portsModel.update(msg)
100			return m, cmd
101	
102		// The terminal focus reaches the ports poll on every tab: its tick runs
103		// whichever tab shows.
104		case shared.TerminalFocusMsg:
105			var cmd tea.Cmd
106			m.portsModel, cmd = m.portsModel.update(msg)
107			return m, cmd
108	
109		// Two tabs now ask before they act — Ports before a kill (§3.26), Forward
110		// before dropping the connections a redirection is carrying — so the answer
111		// goes to the tab that asked rather than to Ports unconditionally, which
112		// would have confirmed a kill from the Forward tab's modal.
113		case components.ConfirmModalYesMsg, components.ConfirmModalNoMsg:
114			return m.routeConfirm(msg)
115	
116		// Forward sub-model messages. ChangedMsg is the router's broadcast, and it
117		// reaches this view wherever it stands, on screen or not.
118		case forward.ChangedMsg, forwardTickMsg, ForwardFormSubmitMsg, ForwardFormCancelMsg:
119			var cmd tea.Cmd
120			m.forwardModel, cmd = m.forwardModel.update(msg)
121			return m, cmd
122	
123		// Topology sub-model messages
124		case ifaceDataMsg:
125			var cmd tea.Cmd
126			m.interfacesModel, cmd = m.interfacesModel.update(msg)
127			return m, cmd
128	
129		case tea.KeyPressMsg:
130			return m.handleKey(msg)
131	
132		case tea.PasteMsg:
133			return m.handlePaste(msg)
134		}
135	
136		// Each tab holds its own footer, so an expiry has to be offered to all
137		// four: the timer fires wherever the user has since navigated.
138		m.footer.Handle(msg)
139		m.portsModel.footer.Handle(msg)
140		m.interfacesModel.footer.Handle(msg)
141		m.forwardModel.footer.Handle(msg)
142		return m, nil
143	}

145	// routeConfirm hands a confirmation answer to the tab that put the modal up.
146	func (m *Model) routeConfirm(msg tea.Msg) (*Model, tea.Cmd) {
147		var cmd tea.Cmd
148		if m.activeTab == tabForward {
149			m.forwardModel, cmd = m.forwardModel.update(msg)
150			return m, cmd
151		}
152		m.portsModel, cmd = m.portsModel.update(msg)
153		return m, cmd
154	}
155	
156	// handleStageDone records one stage's answers and starts the next.
157	func (m *Model) handleStageDone(msg stageDoneMsg) (*Model, tea.Cmd) {
158		if msg.gen != m.runGen {
159			return m, nil // a superseded run
160		}
161		m.results = msg.results
162		m.rebuildChecksTable()
163	
164		steps := netcheck.Steps()
165		if msg.next >= len(steps) {
166			m.state = StateResults
167			m.verdict = netcheck.Summarize(m.results.All())
168			log.Printf("INFO [netdiag] run finished: verdict=%s over %d checks",
169				m.verdict, len(m.results.All()))
170			return m, nil
171		}
172	
173		m.runStep = msg.next
174		m.runStage = steps[msg.next]
175	
176		tg, err := m.buildTarget()
177		if err != nil {
178			// The form has not changed since the run started, so this cannot
179			// normally fail. Reporting it beats continuing with a target nobody
180			// can name.
181			log.Printf("ERROR [netdiag] target became invalid mid-run: %v", err)
182			m.state = StateResults
183			return m, m.footer.Error("Run stopped — the target is no longer valid")
184		}
185		return m, runStageCmd(m.runGen, tg, m.checkSettings(), msg.next, m.results)
186	}

188	// handlePaste gives pasted text to the field that has the keyboard on the tab on
189	// screen. It never reaches the key handlers, so no action fires (Rule 111).
190	func (m *Model) handlePaste(msg tea.PasteMsg) (*Model, tea.Cmd) {
191		var cmd tea.Cmd
192		switch m.activeTab {
193		case tabPorts:
194			m.portsModel, cmd = m.portsModel.update(msg)
195		case tabInterfaces:
196			m.interfacesModel, cmd = m.interfacesModel.update(msg)
197		case tabForward:
198			m.forwardModel, cmd = m.forwardModel.update(msg)
199		default:
200			switch {
201			case m.filterBar.InEditMode():
202				m.filterBar, cmd = m.filterBar.Update(msg)
203				m.rebuildChecksTable()
204			case m.state == StateInput:
205				return m.updateActiveInput(msg)
206			}
207		}
208		return m, cmd
209	}

211	func (m *Model) handleKey(msg tea.KeyPressMsg) (*Model, tea.Cmd) {
212		// A filter bar in edit mode claims every key before anything else, or a
213		// query cannot contain the letters the view binds.
214		if m.activeTab == tabDiagnostics && m.filterBar.InEditMode() {
215			var cmd tea.Cmd
216			m.filterBar, cmd = m.filterBar.Update(msg)
217			m.rebuildChecksTable()
218			return m, cmd
219		}
220	
221		// Tab / Shift+Tab cycles between the three tabs (Rule 135)
222		switch msg.String() {
223		case "tab":
224			m.activeTab = (m.activeTab + 1) % tabCount
225			return m, nil
226		case "shift+tab":
227			m.activeTab = (m.activeTab + tabCount - 1) % tabCount
228			return m, nil
229		}
230	
231		// Route to active tab
232		if m.activeTab == tabPorts {
233			var cmd tea.Cmd
234			m.portsModel, cmd = m.portsModel.update(msg)
235			return m, cmd
236		}
237		if m.activeTab == tabInterfaces {
238			var cmd tea.Cmd
239			m.interfacesModel, cmd = m.interfacesModel.update(msg)
240			return m, cmd
241		}
242		if m.activeTab == tabForward {
243			var cmd tea.Cmd
244			m.forwardModel, cmd = m.forwardModel.update(msg)
245			return m, cmd
246		}
247	
248		switch m.state {
249		case StateInput:
250			return m.handleKeyInput(msg)
251		case StateRunning:
252			return m.handleKeyRunning(msg)
253		case StateResults:
254			return m.handleKeyResults(msg)
255		case StateDetails:
256			return m.handleKeyDetails(msg)
257		}
258		return m, nil
259	}
260	
261	// handleKeyRunning cancels the run. The stage in flight is awaited rather than
262	// interrupted — it is a network read that will time out on its own — and its
263	// result is discarded by the generation counter.
264	func (m *Model) handleKeyRunning(msg tea.KeyPressMsg) (*Model, tea.Cmd) {
265		if msg.String() != "esc" {
266			return m, nil
267		}
268		m.runGen++
269		m.state = StateResults
270		m.verdict = netcheck.Summarize(m.results.All())
271		m.rebuildChecksTable()
272		return m, m.footer.Warn("Run cancelled — showing what completed")
273	}
274	
275	func (m *Model) handleKeyInput(msg tea.KeyPressMsg) (*Model, tea.Cmd) {
276		switch msg.String() {
277		case "down":
278			m.moveFocus(1)
279			return m, nil
280		case "up":
281			m.moveFocus(-1)
282			return m, nil
283		case "enter":
284			// enter runs from anywhere in the form: with three fields and one
285			// button there is nothing else it could mean, and making the user walk
286			// to the button first is a step that buys nothing.
287			return m.StartRun()
288		case "esc":
289			return m, nil
290		}
291		return m.updateActiveInput(msg)
292	}

294	func (m *Model) moveFocus(delta int) {
295		switch m.focusedField {
296		case fieldTarget:
297			m.targetInput.Blur()
298		case fieldPort:
299			m.portInput.Blur()
300		case fieldDNSServer:
301			m.dnsServerInput.Blur()
302		}
303	
304		m.focusedField = (m.focusedField + delta + fieldCount) % fieldCount
305	
306		switch m.focusedField {
307		case fieldTarget:
308			m.targetInput.Focus()
309		case fieldPort:
310			m.portInput.Focus()
311		case fieldDNSServer:
312			m.dnsServerInput.Focus()
313		}
314	}
315	
316	func (m *Model) updateActiveInput(msg tea.Msg) (*Model, tea.Cmd) {
317		var cmd tea.Cmd
318		switch m.focusedField {
319		case fieldTarget:
320			m.targetInput, cmd = m.targetInput.Update(msg)
321		case fieldPort:
322			m.portInput, cmd = m.portInput.Update(msg)
323		case fieldDNSServer:
324			m.dnsServerInput, cmd = m.dnsServerInput.Update(msg)
325		}
326		return m, cmd
327	}
328	
329	func (m *Model) handleKeyResults(msg tea.KeyPressMsg) (*Model, tea.Cmd) {
330		switch msg.String() {
331		case "enter":
332			return m.openDetails()
333		case "esc":
334			// No origin view means netdiag was opened directly (the command
335			// line), so esc stays inside it and resets to the form, as it
336			// always has. An origin means it was opened prefilled from
337			// elsewhere (status's H, §3.66), and esc returns there instead.
338			if m.OriginView == "" {
339				return m.resetToForm()
340			}
341			origin := m.OriginView
342			return m, func() tea.Msg { return BackToOriginMsg{Origin: origin} }
343		case "ctrl+r":
344			return m.StartRun()
345		case "/":
346			return m, m.filterBar.ActivateSearch()
347		case "p":
348			m.filterBar.SetTokenActive(problemsToken, !m.filterBar.IsTokenActive(problemsToken))
349			m.rebuildChecksTable()
350			return m, nil
351		case keymap.New:
352			// Always resets to the form, regardless of OriginView — the one way
353			// to run a wholly new diagnostic without first leaving to wherever
354			// this run was opened from. Found missing the day §3.66 shipped H:
355			// esc alone left no way back to the form once an origin was set, and
356			// re-entering netdiag through the command line landed on the same
357			// frozen results with the same problem, since the cached view (and
358			// its OriginView) is reused rather than rebuilt.
359			return m.resetToForm()
360		}
361		return m, m.checksTable.Update(msg)
362	}
363	
364	func (m *Model) handleKeyDetails(msg tea.KeyPressMsg) (*Model, tea.Cmd) {
365		switch msg.String() {
366		case "esc":
367			m.state = StateResults
368			return m, nil
369		case "up":
370			m.detailsViewport.ScrollUp(1)
371		case "down":
372			m.detailsViewport.ScrollDown(1)
373		case "pgup":
374			m.detailsViewport.HalfPageUp()
375		case "pgdown":
376			m.detailsViewport.HalfPageDown()
377		case "home":
378			m.detailsViewport.GotoTop()
379		case "end":
380			m.detailsViewport.GotoBottom()
381		}
382		return m, nil
383	}
384	
385	func (m *Model) openDetails() (*Model, tea.Cmd) {
386		c, ok := m.checksTable.Selected()
387		if !ok {
388			return m, nil
389		}
390		m.selected = c
391		m.state = StateDetails
392		m.resizeDetailsViewport()
393		m.detailsViewport.SetContent(m.renderDetailsContent(m.detailsViewport.Width()))
394		m.detailsViewport.GotoTop()
395		return m, nil
396	}
397	
398	func (m *Model) resetToForm() (*Model, tea.Cmd) {
399		m.state = StateInput
400		m.focusedField = fieldTarget
401		m.targetInput.Focus()
402		m.results = netcheck.Results{}
403		m.verdict = netcheck.Unknown
404		m.filterBar.ClearSearch()
405		m.filterBar.SetTokenActive(problemsToken, false)
406		m.rebuildChecksTable()
407		// Starting over severs the tie to wherever this run was opened from: the
408		// next run is not "the monitor status sent here" anymore, so esc on its
409		// results should not try to leave for a view this new target has nothing
410		// to do with.
411		m.OriginView = ""
412		return m, nil
413	}

# TUI — Bubble Tea behavior & architecture

### Rule 109 : Bubble Tea message naming convention

- Format: `[ComponentName][Action]Msg`
- Examples: `ComponentFormSubmitMsg`, `ConfirmModalYesMsg`
- Always document with a comment
- Group related messages together in the file

### Rule 110 : NEVER modify the model inside a Cmd ⚠️

**Fundamental principle of Bubble Tea (Elm architecture).**

`Update()`, `View()`, and `Cmd`s execute in parallel. Modifying the model inside a Cmd creates race conditions detectable with `go run -race`.

| Component | Role | Can modify the model? |
|-----------|------|---------------------------|
| `Update()` | Processes messages | ✅ YES (the only allowed place) |
| `View()` | Renders the UI | ❌ NO (read-only) |
| `Cmd` | Async I/O operations | ❌ NO (returns messages) |

```go
// ❌ WRONG — race condition
func (m *Model) logout() tea.Cmd {
    return func() tea.Msg {
        m.authenticated = false  // DANGER
        return nil
    }
}

// ✅ CORRECT — message + Update()
type LogoutCompleteMsg struct{}

func (m *Model) logout() tea.Cmd {
    url := m.urlInput.Value()  // copy the data we need
    return func() tea.Msg {
        auth := gitlabpkg.NewAuth(m.storage)
        _ = auth.Logout(url)
        return LogoutCompleteMsg{}
    }
}

case LogoutCompleteMsg:
    m.authenticated = false  // thread-safe inside Update()
    m.user = nil
    return m, nil
```

**Golden rule**: Cmds do the "dirty work" (I/O), then send a message to `Update()`.

### Rule 126 : Scan cache behavior (Images & Workspaces)

| Action | Disk cache | Memory cache | Scan triggered |
|--------|-------------|---------------|------------|
| `Enter` (scanned item) | Read | Read | No |
| `Enter` (not scanned) | — | — | No |
| `ctrl+s` (in progress) | Blocked | Blocked | No |
| `ctrl+s` (available) | Overwritten | Updated | Yes (item only) |
| `A` (unscanned) | Unchanged | Unchanged | Yes (unscanned) |
| `ctrl+a` (all) | **Purged** | **Purged** | Yes (all) |

**`ctrl+a` must clear the cache before relaunching the scans:**
```go
// ✅ CORRECT
func (m Model) requestScanAll() (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {
    var keys []string
    for _, img := range m.images {
        delete(m.scanCache, name)  // in-memory purge inside Update()
        keys = append(keys, name)
    }
    return m, tea.Batch(deleteScanCacheCmd(keys), batchScanCmd(keys, m.defaultScanOpts()))
}
```

### Rule 128 : Footer messages — three levels, centered, one component

**`components.FooterMessage` is the only implementation.** A view does not
render its own message: it declares one, sets it from `Update()`, and
renders it via `m.footer.View(width, status)`.

There used to be eight of them, one per view, each with its own fields,
timer, and lipgloss block. That is what produced the flaw this component
removes: nobody ever centered the error branch, in any of the eight, so
errors were left-aligned everywhere while notices were centered.

#### The three levels

They are defined by **what happened**, not by how it feels:

| Level | Meaning | Color |
|--------|------|---------|
| `Error` | an operation failed, or the system refused it | `ColorFooterError` = the red of **CRITICAL** CVEs |
| `Warn` | the action cannot be honored as requested, but nothing failed: an unmet precondition, already in progress, not applicable here | `ColorFooterWarn` = the orange of **MEDIUM** CVEs |
| `Info` | a neutral fact, or a successful operation | `ColorFooterInfo` = `ColorText`, the ordinary text color |

Info is not bold, the other two are: the hierarchy runs through weight as
much as through hue, and a neutral info in bold would turn back into an
alert.

The colors are **semantic aliases** assigned in `ApplyTheme` (`colors.go`),
like the viewer's syntax colors: no theme file gains a key. They target the
**severity** names rather than `ColorError` / `ColorWarn` — the default
theme makes them coincide, so the choice is invisible today; it stops being
invisible in a theme that separates them.

#### What is forbidden

- ❌ `theme.StatusErrorStyle`, `StatusOKStyle`, `StatusWarningStyle`, or
  `ColorHighlight` inside a `RenderFooter`, a `renderInfoLine`, or a
  `renderInfoText` — `TestNoViewStylesItsOwnFooterMessage` scans the sources
  and fails, naming the file, line, and function.
- ❌ **Green** in a footer. It is reserved for status icons (Rule 121).
- ❌ A **left-aligned** message. `View` centers, always, across the full
  width.
- ❌ A local timer (`clearFooterCmd`, `clearInfoMsgCmd`, …): the component
  carries it.

#### Mandatory pattern

```go
// 1. The model declares a field.
type Model struct {
    footer sharedcomponents.FooterMessage
}

// 2. Update() sets the message and returns its timer. A message set without
//    its timer never disappears.
case SomeErrorMsg:
    log.Printf("ERROR [package/view] action: %v", msg.Err)
    return m, m.footer.Error("Failed to load data — check logs")

case ScanAlreadyRunningMsg:
    return m, m.footer.Warn("Scan already in progress")

// 3. Update() offers unhandled messages to the component, which consumes
//    the expiry addressed to it.
m.footer.Handle(msg)
return m, nil

// 4. RenderFooter() renders the line, blank included — Rule 124 budgets it.
func (m Model) RenderFooter(width int) string {
    return theme.EmptyLineBg(width) + "
" + m.footer.View(width, m.status())
}
```

**The expiry carries an id** (`ClearFooterMsg{ID}`): a stale timer does not
clear the message that took its predecessor's place. That is what makes the
type shareable across packages, and it fixes, in passing, a flaw all eight
implementations shared — a message set at t+2.9s was cleared at t+3s by the
previous one's timer.

#### `Status` — what has no timer

A progress indicator, a hint, a loading state: these are **states**, not
events. They are derived on every frame and passed as `View`'s second
argument, never set as a message — a line set when the first repo starts
would be cleared while the tenth is still running.

```go
func (m Model) status() sharedcomponents.Status {
    if m.loading && len(m.table.Items()) == 0 {
        // the view's own load: the shared dot, with WantsBlink
        return sharedcomponents.Status{Text: "Loading images...", Activity: true}
    }
    // work the router tracks (a run in the registry): the shared dot
    return sharedcomponents.Status{Text: m.progressLine(), Activity: m.anyRunning()}
}
```

Precedence in `View`: **error → warning → info → status**. A failure the
user has not read takes priority over the progress of whatever is still
running.

One field prefixes the line with a mark:

| Field | Mark | Use it for | Driven by |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Activity: true` | the shared activity dot, `●` / `○` (same glyph and colour as the row dots, `indicator.Running`) | any loading or running state: work the **router tracks** (a run in the jobs registry) and a view's own load (`WantsBlink()`) | the router's 500 ms blink phase: the view calls `m.footer.SetBlinkPhase(msg.Blink)` from its `jobs.FrameMsg` handler |

The braille spinner is removed (DEVDESK-377): `Status.Spinner`,
`FooterMessage.SetSpinnerFrame`, `theme.SpinnerMessage` and
`theme.SpinnerStyle` no longer exist, and no file under `internal/` may import
`charm.land/bubbles/v2/spinner`. `TestNoViewImportsTheBubblesSpinner` and
`TestRemovedSpinnerSymbolsStayGone` (`internal/app/activity_guard_test.go`)
fail on a reintroduction, with no exception. `dk setup` has no router: it shows
a fixed `●` and the pending text, with no blink. Without a `SetBlinkPhase`
call the dot is steady on. `●` and `○` are one column wide and share a width,
so the phase never shifts the text.

A future `Activity` value that does not depend on the jobs registry must make
its view implement `WantsBlink() bool` (return `status().Activity`, as the
forge explorer does); otherwise the router arms no animation chain and the dot
stays fixed on `●`.

#### A table's loading state belongs to the footer

**When a `datatable` is loading, the table stays on screen** and the
loading state is an info message with a mark (the shared activity dot, for the
view's own load as well as for work the router tracks), in the footer only. A body that replaces itself with a loading screen loses its header and columns for the
duration of every `ctrl+r`, then regains them: a layout jump on every
refresh.

**A footer mark is for a table's data loading, never for one row.**
What is happening to a single row (a scan, a clone, a stop) is that row's
activity dot (Rule 125, "The activity column"); when the selected row has a
footer detail with a glyph (`Detail.Glyph`), the footer shows no dot: the
row's own dot already moves.

Mandatory consequence: the empty message ("No images found") is
**conditioned on loading being finished**, otherwise the table announces the
absence of what it is still looking for.

`TestNoTableViewRendersALoadingBody` (`internal/ui/components`) rejects a
loading body in the table views it covers. There is no declared exception.

#### Tests — the timer really does sleep

`tea.Tick` blocks for its entire duration, and `testutil.Msgs` runs the
whole batch it is given: a test that inspects a `Cmd` carrying the timer
pays the full three seconds.

- To verify that a message **disappears**, build the expiry rather than
  running the `Cmd`:
  `feed(t, m, components.ClearFooterMsg{ID: m.footer.ID()})`.
- For a test that must drain the `Cmd` (because it is looking for another
  one inside it), shorten the timer:
  `testutil.FastTimers(t, &components.FooterMsgDuration)`.

`FooterMsgDuration` is an exported `var` for this reason alone; its
production value is fixed by `TestAMessageGetsThreeSeconds`.

#### Other prohibitions

Mandatory log format: `log.Printf("ERROR [package/view] action: %v", err)`

- ❌ `err.Error()` directly in the UI (except a validation message already
  written to be read)
- ❌ Replacing the view with an error screen (except fatal initialization
  errors)
- ❌ Ignoring an error without `log.Printf`

  `ColorHighlight` inside a `RenderFooter`, a `renderInfoLine`, or a
  `renderInfoText` — `TestNoViewStylesItsOwnFooterMessage` scans the sources
  and fails, naming the file, line, and function.
- ❌ **Green** in a footer. It is reserved for status icons (Rule 121).
- ❌ A **left-aligned** message. `View` centers, always, across the full
  width.
- ❌ A local timer (`clearFooterCmd`, `clearInfoMsgCmd`, …): the component
  carries it.

#### Mandatory pattern

```go
// 1. The model declares a field.
type Model struct {
    footer sharedcomponents.FooterMessage
}

// 2. Update() sets the message and returns its timer. A message set without
//    its timer never disappears.
case SomeErrorMsg:
    log.Printf("ERROR [package/view] action: %v", msg.Err)
    return m, m.footer.Error("Failed to load data — check logs")

case ScanAlreadyRunningMsg:
    return m, m.footer.Warn("Scan already in progress")

// 3. Update() offers unhandled messages to the component, which consumes
//    the expiry addressed to it.
m.footer.Handle(msg)
return m, nil

// 4. RenderFooter() renders the line, blank included — Rule 124 budgets it.
func (m Model) RenderFooter(width int) string {
    return theme.EmptyLineBg(width) + "
" + m.footer.View(width, m.status())
}
```

**The expiry carries an id** (`ClearFooterMsg{ID}`): a stale timer does not
clear the message that took its predecessor's place. That is what makes the
type shareable across packages, and it fixes, in passing, a flaw all eight
implementations shared — a message set at t+2.9s was cleared at t+3s by the
previous one's timer.

#### `Status` — what has no timer

A progress indicator, a hint, a loading state: these are **states**, not
events. They are derived on every frame and passed as `View`'s second
argument, never set as a message — a line set when the first repo starts
would be cleared while the tenth is still running.

```go
func (m Model) status() sharedcomponents.Status {
    if m.loading && len(m.table.Items()) == 0 {
        // the view's own load: the shared dot, with WantsBlink
        return sharedcomponents.Status{Text: "Loading images...", Activity: true}
    }
    // work the router tracks (a run in the registry): the shared dot
    return sharedcomponents.Status{Text: m.progressLine(), Activity: m.anyRunning()}
}
```

Precedence in `View`: **error → warning → info → status**. A failure the
user has not read takes priority over the progress of whatever is still
running.

One field prefixes the line with a mark:

| Field | Mark | Use it for | Driven by |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Activity: true` | the shared activity dot, `●` / `○` (same glyph and colour as the row dots, `indicator.Running`) | any loading or running state: work the **router tracks** (a run in the jobs registry) and a view's own load (`WantsBlink()`) | the router's 500 ms blink phase: the view calls `m.footer.SetBlinkPhase(msg.Blink)` from its `jobs.FrameMsg` handler |

The braille spinner is removed (DEVDESK-377): `Status.Spinner`,
`FooterMessage.SetSpinnerFrame`, `theme.SpinnerMessage` and
`theme.SpinnerStyle` no longer exist, and no file under `internal/` may import
`charm.land/bubbles/v2/spinner`. `TestNoViewImportsTheBubblesSpinner` and
`TestRemovedSpinnerSymbolsStayGone` (`internal/app/activity_guard_test.go`)
fail on a reintroduction, with no exception. `dk setup` has no router: it shows
a fixed `●` and the pending text, with no blink. Without a `SetBlinkPhase`
call the dot is steady on. `●` and `○` are one column wide and share a width,
so the phase never shifts the text.

A future `Activity` value that does not depend on the jobs registry must make
its view implement `WantsBlink() bool` (return `status().Activity`, as the
forge explorer does); otherwise the router arms no animation chain and the dot
stays fixed on `●`.

#### A table's loading state belongs to the footer

**When a `datatable` is loading, the table stays on screen** and the
loading state is an info message with a mark (the shared activity dot, for the
view's own load as well as for work the router tracks), in the footer only. A body that replaces itself with a loading screen loses its header and columns for the
duration of every `ctrl+r`, then regains them: a layout jump on every
refresh.

**A footer mark is for a table's data loading, never for one row.**
What is happening to a single row (a scan, a clone, a stop) is that row's
activity dot (Rule 125, "The activity column"); when the selected row has a
footer detail with a glyph (`Detail.Glyph`), the footer shows no dot: the
row's own dot already moves.

Mandatory consequence: the empty message ("No images found") is
**conditioned on loading being finished**, otherwise the table announces the
absence of what it is still looking for.

`TestNoTableViewRendersALoadingBody` (`internal/ui/components`) rejects a
loading body in the table views it covers. There is no declared exception.

#### Tests — the timer really does sleep

`tea.Tick` blocks for its entire duration, and `testutil.Msgs` runs the
whole batch it is given: a test that inspects a `Cmd` carrying the timer
pays the full three seconds.

- To verify that a message **disappears**, build the expiry rather than
  running the `Cmd`:
  `feed(t, m, components.ClearFooterMsg{ID: m.footer.ID()})`.
- For a test that must drain the `Cmd` (because it is looking for another
  one inside it), shorten the timer:
  `testutil.FastTimers(t, &components.FooterMsgDuration)`.

`FooterMsgDuration` is an exported `var` for this reason alone; its
production value is fixed by `TestAMessageGetsThreeSeconds`.

#### Other prohibitions

Mandatory log format: `log.Printf("ERROR [package/view] action: %v", err)`

- ❌ `err.Error()` directly in the UI (except a validation message already
  written to be read)
- ❌ Replacing the view with an error screen (except fatal initialization
  errors)
- ❌ Ignoring an error without `log.Printf`

</system-reminder>
